Hacker — Modern occupation profile adapted from the supplied community reference.

Income: Lower to Upper Lower class

Contacts: Other hackers, usually anonymously

Occupation skills: Computer Use, Electrical Repair, Electronics, Fast Talk, Internet Use, Library Use, Language (Any), Science (Physics), Programming.

Legacy conversions: Other Language → Language (Any); Physics → Science (Physics).

Original special notes (Keeper review): -1 APP , +20 Computer Use. Hackers are uncomfortable in social situations, even though they are frequently charismatic and able to manipulate people. They often have a strong fear, distrust, or hatred of the government and law enforcement. Keep in mind that this is the early 90s, when everything was vulnerable, and that the Keeper of this particular campaign has a strong understanding of hackers’ capabilities.

Community-reference adaptation; review credit rating and skill selections for your campaign.

v0.4 homebrew occupation points: EDU × 2 + INT × 2. This is an adaptation, not a verified official formula. Original special abilities, if any, remain descriptive only.
Additional homebrew skill for the Universal Occupations module. Internet Use is not in the supplied CoC7 system skill registry. Base chance: 20% (Keeper-adjustable).
Additional homebrew skill for the Universal Occupations module. Programming is not in the supplied CoC7 system skill registry. Base chance: 5% (Keeper-adjustable).

Programmer — Modern occupation profile adapted from the supplied community reference.

Income: Lower to Middle class (this was before programmers became a huge commodity).

Contacts: Other programmers, hackers, customers

Occupation skills: Accounting, Computer Use, Electrical Repair, Electronics, Fast Talk, Internet Use, Library Use, Language (Any), Programming, Science (Any).

Legacy conversions: Other Language → Language (Any); up to 2 areas of specialization. → Science (Any).

Original special notes (Keeper review): -1 APP , -1 SIZ , -1 CON . +1d20 + 40 to Programming, +20 to Computer Use. Programmers are uncomfortable in social situations, and usually work for educational institutions or in scientific endeavours. May have access to source for both civilian and military projects, and may be able to build in backdoors.
